newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's CIB 1996 net profit up 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's CIB 1996 net profit up 11 pct.

text.p: Egypt's retail Commercial International Bank said on Sunday it had increased net profits for calendar 1996 by almost 11 percent to 241.3 million pounds ($70.9 million) from 217.7 million in 1995.
The bank said in a faxed statement that net assets also rose to 10.96 billion pounds in 1996 from 7.78 billion in the previous year.
Investment income was also higher at 4.4 million from 0.28 million in 1995.
CIB is one of the banking sector's most active stocks. It issued Egypt's first global depositary receipt offering which is now trading on the SEAQ in London.

The faxed balance sheet did not specify how the profit would be distributed and what the dividend will be for its 50 million shares. On Sunday, the shares were trading down at 83.95 pounds from Thursday's close of 88.32.
Earlier this month, the bank applied for a $100 million three-year syndicated loan, the first by an Egyptian borrower for 15 years.
